title: Detection of Bordetella pertussis Vaccine Antigens by ELISA
author: Nora Zidane
materials: Primary antibodies *A mixture of the two monoclonal antibodies 99/512 and 99/542 is used. Recommendations: For the treatment of a complete 96-well samples plate, provide 2 mL of primary Ab diluted in TB for each of the antibodies. For the treatment of a 96-well standard range plate, provide 2.5 mL of primary Ab diluted in TB for each of the antibodies. Keep the Ab in the ice. Gently mix them by hand then quickly centrifuge with the minispin.
PT positive, PRN negative, FHA negative , FIM3
Anti-FHA antibodies diluted in the TB (1/2
Anti-PRN antibodies diluted in the TB (1/1
Anti-FIM2 antibodies diluted in the TB (1/10
Anti-FIM3 antibodies diluted in the TB (1/10

steps.title: Prepare 1X PBS solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve one PBS tablet in 200 mL distilled water, filter, and store at +4 ± 5 °C for up to one month. For a 96‑well plate, prepare 50 mL of PBS 1X.

steps.title: Prepare washing buffer (0.05% Tween)
steps.instruction: Mix 0.5 mL Tween 20 with 1000 mL physiological water to obtain 0.05 % Tween. For a 96‑well plate, prepare 250 mL. Keep the viscous detergent away from light.

steps.title: Prepare blocking/saturation buffer (TB)
steps.instruction: Combine 5 g skim milk with 100 mL PBS 1X (5 % w/v) and make up to 100 mL. For the complete treatment (saturation, primary Ab, secondary Ab) of a 96‑well plate, prepare 50 mL of TB.

steps.title: Prepare TMB substrate working solution
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of TMB Substrate A and TMB Substrate B (v/v) to obtain the working solution; prepare only the volume needed, protect from light, and keep at room temperature.

steps.title: Equilibrate reagents to room temperature
steps.instruction: Remove all solutions and reagents from the refrigerator at least 30 min before use and keep them at room temperature during the assay to avoid slowing reactions.

steps.title: Prepare antigen dilutions in plate
steps.instruction: Dilute each antigen to 1.0 µg mL⁻¹ in PBS 1X (1 : 50). In a 96‑well plate add 100 µL PBS to columns 2‑12, add 200 µL antigen to column 1 (duplicate wells), transfer 100 µL from column 1 to column 2, and continue serial 1 : 2 dilutions across columns 3‑12. Discard 100 µL from column 12 so that each well contains 100 µL. Aliquot mother solutions, mix gently, centrifuge briefly with a Minispin, and keep antigens on ice to avoid denaturation.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial suspensions for coating
steps.instruction: Grow each B. pertussis strain on BGS medium, suspend cells in physiological water to an OD₆₅₀ = 1.0. Aliquot 400 µL of each suspension into low‑binding Eppendorf tubes, centrifuge 10 min at 10 °C, 8000 rpm, label tubes (OD4), remove all supernatant with a micropipette, and store the pellets at –20 °C or proceed directly to inactivation.

steps.title: Thermal inactivation and dilution to OD0.2
steps.instruction: Resuspend each OD4 pellet in 400 µL physiological water, heat at 56 °C for 1 h in a dry bath, then dilute 1 : 5 with PBS to obtain OD₆₅₀ = 0.2. Prepare 1500 µL final volume per sample by mixing 300 µL inactivated suspension with 1200 µL PBS 1X.

steps.title: Coat ELISA plate with bacterial suspensions
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the OD₆₅₀ = 0.2 suspension to wells in columns 1‑10 of each row (same sample across the row). Test five virulence factors (PT, FHA, PRN, FIM2, FIM3) in duplicate (10 wells per sample). Use rows A‑F for up to six samples. Add a positive‑control line (row G) with two Tohama wells per factor (10 wells) and a negative‑control line (row H) with two PBS wells per factor (10 wells). Prepare a separate standard‑range plate for PT, FHA and PRN using purified antigens (no standards for FIM2/3). Cover plates with film and incubate overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash plate three times
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL washing buffer to each well, discard, and repeat for a total of three washes.

steps.title: Block plate with TB
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL blocking/saturation buffer (TB) to each well and incubate 1 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash plate post‑block
steps.instruction: Perform three washes with 200 µL washing buffer per well as described above.

steps.title: Add primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Dispense 100 µL of the appropriate primary antibody into each well according to the plate plan: anti‑PT (1 : 1000 in TB), anti‑FHA (1 : 2000 in TB), anti‑PRN (1 : 1000 in TB), anti‑FIM2 (1 : 10 000 in TB), anti‑FIM3 (1 : 10 000 in TB).

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with fresh film, seal tightly, and incubate 2 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash plate post‑primary
steps.instruction: Wash three times with 200 µL washing buffer per well.

steps.title: Add secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of secondary antibody diluted 1 : 1000 in TB to each well.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 2 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash plate post‑secondary
steps.instruction: Wash three times with 200 µL washing buffer per well.

steps.title: Add TMB substrate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the prepared TMB substrate to each well (protect from light).

steps.title: Develop color reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Stop reaction
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL STOP solution to each well.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Read each well at 450 nm (signal) and 570 nm (background) using a Multiskan plate reader.

steps.title: Analyze ELISA results
steps.instruction: For each well subtract the 570 nm value from the 450 nm value. Calculate the mean and standard deviation of duplicate wells. Consider a sample positive when the mean absorbance is >0.2 for PT, FHA, PRN or >0.3 for FIM2, FIM3. Quantify positives using the standard curve; calculations may be performed with MyAssays (https://www.myassays.com).
